sectionProgressions.progression: Single-Note A Blues Riff into A5
sectionProgressions.description: The winding John Paul Jones-penned single-note riff ending on an authoritative A5 power chord
Driving rock shuffle under 'Hey, hey baby, said the way you move'
Page's legendary multi-tracked Les Paul solo over a relentless driving rhythm section

harmonicFunction: A5 (I5) - Primal rock tonic anchor providing immovable resolution after the winding riff
E5 (V5) - Dominant power chord driving the turnaround in the chorus
D5 (IV5) - Subdominant chord completing the classic rock 12-bar power structure

techniques.name: Complex Metric Syncopation & Triple-Tracked Overdrive
techniques.description: Navigating shifting metric accents where the guitar riff weaves around a steady 4/4 drum beat with deceptive start and stop points

notes: Riff starts on fret 5 of low E (A root) and ascends through the blues scale
Hammer-ons and pull-offs on the D and G strings (frets 5, 6, and 7)
Sudden syncopated rest before hitting the crashing A5 power chord
sequence: Wait for Plant's vocal phrase to finish
Enter on the upbeat of beat 4 with the low E string walkup
Execute the sixteenth-note winding blues line across strings 5, 4, and 3
Drop heavily on the resolving A5 power chord (fret 5 low E barre)
tips: Count in 4/4 without getting thrown by the riff's unexpected syncopations—Bonham plays straight 4/4 drums throughout
Page achieved the unique fuzzy crackle by plugging his Les Paul straight into a mic preamp channel on a Universal Audio console with 1176 limiting
Triple-track your rhythm guitars for that massive wall of sound

sections.name: Main Winding Riff
sections.description: One of the most rhythmically intricate and famous guitar riffs in rock history.
notes: Enter cleanly after the vocal cue
Crisp alternate picking on the sixteenth notes
Slam the final A5 power chord with full authority

sections.name: Chorus Shuffle
sections.description: The hard-driving rock shuffle supporting 'Hey hey mama said the way you move'.
notes: Lock tight with Bonham's snare backbeat
Palm mute slightly on the low E pedal notes

sections.name: Outro Solo Extravaganza
sections.description: Jimmy Page's legendary layered guitar solo over the relentless driving rhythm track.
notes: Rapid 5th-position A minor pentatonic blues runs
Wild string bends with rapid finger vibrato

guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker (PAF) for cutting high-mid direct punch

amp.recommended: Direct into Universal Audio 610 tube console / Marshall 1959 Super Lead 100W

effects.distortion: Universal Audio dual 1176 limiting amplifiers in series for fuzz-compression
effects.reverb: Headley Grange stone stairwell natural acoustics

beginner.title: A5 Rock Chords & Rhythm
steps: Master the A5, E5, and D5 power chord shapes
Learn to play in time with a straight 4/4 drum beat at 82 BPM

intermediate.title: The Main Riff Notes
steps: Learn the exact note sequence of the main riff at half speed (50 BPM)
Practice counting the metric entry point after the vocal cue
Bring the riff up to album tempo of 82 BPM with metronome

advanced.title: Metric Fluency & Outro Solo
steps: Play the main riff locked perfectly with John Bonham's straight 4/4 drum groove
Learn Page's multi-layered outro solo licks in the 5th position
Capture the authentic aggressive pick attack and direct-to-board fuzz bite

commonMistakes: Trying to count the riff in 5/4 or 6/4—the drum beat is straight 4/4 throughout
Entering too early or late after the a cappella vocal line
Fumbling the rapid string crossing on the 4th and 5th strings
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Isolated main riff at 60 BPM with metronome
5 minutes: Speed buildup to 82 BPM locking with drum track
5 minutes: Outro solo blues lick articulation in 5th position
metronomeWork: Keep metronome strictly on 4/4 at 82 BPM
Do not stop the metronome during the vocal breaks—learn where the downbeats land
